questiontext.text:
\(A\) is \(({@A[1]@}, {@A[2]@})\) and \(B\) is \(({@B[1]@}, {@B[2]@})\).

Condition 1: \(PA\) [[if test="is(st=1)"]]\(\lt\)[[else]]\(\le\)[[/if]] \({@r@}\).

Condition 2: \(P\) is nearer to [[if test="is(sd=0)"]]\(A\) than to \(B\)[[else]]\(B\) than to \(A\)[[/if]].

For each point \(P\), decide which conditions it satisfies.

  1. \(({@P[1][1]@}, {@P[1][2]@})\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
  2. \(({@P[2][1]@}, {@P[2][2]@})\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]
  3. \(({@P[3][1]@}, {@P[3][2]@})\) [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt3]]
  4. \(({@P[4][1]@}, {@P[4][2]@})\) [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt4]]

generalfeedback.text:
Condition 1 compares \(PA^2\) with \({@r@}^2 = {@r^2@}\). A point exactly \({@r@}\) from \(A\) is on the circle: [[if test="is(st=1)"]]it does not satisfy \(PA \lt {@r@}\)[[else]]it does satisfy \(PA \le {@r@}\)[[/if]]. Condition 2 compares \(PA^2\) with \(PB^2\). A point on the perpendicular bisector of \(AB\) is the same distance from both, so it is nearer to neither.

  1. \(({@P[1][1]@}, {@P[1][2]@})\): \(PA^2 = {@pa2[1]@}\), \(PB^2 = {@pb2[1]@}\). Condition 1 [[if test="c1l[1]"]]holds[[else]]fails[[/if]]; condition 2 [[if test="c2l[1]"]]holds[[else]]fails[[/if]].

  2. \(({@P[2][1]@}, {@P[2][2]@})\): \(PA^2 = {@pa2[2]@}\), \(PB^2 = {@pb2[2]@}\). Condition 1 [[if test="c1l[2]"]]holds[[else]]fails[[/if]]; condition 2 [[if test="c2l[2]"]]holds[[else]]fails[[/if]].

  3. \(({@P[3][1]@}, {@P[3][2]@})\): \(PA^2 = {@pa2[3]@}\), \(PB^2 = {@pb2[3]@}\). Condition 1 [[if test="c1l[3]"]]holds[[else]]fails[[/if]]; condition 2 [[if test="c2l[3]"]]holds[[else]]fails[[/if]].

  4. \(({@P[4][1]@}, {@P[4][2]@})\): \(PA^2 = {@pa2[4]@}\), \(PB^2 = {@pb2[4]@}\). Condition 1 [[if test="c1l[4]"]]holds[[else]]fails[[/if]]; condition 2 [[if test="c2l[4]"]]holds[[else]]fails[[/if]].

questiondescription.text:
Loci: which conditions a point satisfies

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.3: Test points, including boundary points, against a distance condition and an equidistance condition.

Core

This question is original to this project.
